recipes.name: Homemade Fresh Pumpkin Pie
ingredients_raw: 3 tablespoons cold water, or more as needed
0.5 teaspoon ground cinnamon, or more to taste
0.5 teaspoon ground ginger, or more to taste
0.5 teaspoon ground nutmeg, or more to taste

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
To make the pastry crust: Mix flour and salt together in a bowl. Cut in butter with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Mix in 3 tablespoons water, one at a time, until dough is moist enough to hold together. Add up to 1 more tablespoon water if needed.
Shape dough into a ball with lightly floured hands. Roll dough on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Place a 9-inch pie pan upside-down on the dough; use a sharp knife to cut a circle of dough 1 ½ inches larger than the pie pan. Remove and discard dough scraps and set pie pan aside.
Gently roll circular piece of dough around the rolling pin; transfer it right-side up over the pie pan. Unroll, easing dough into the bottom of the pan.
Use two hands to flute the dough around the top edges.
To make the filling: Beat pumpkin, evaporated milk, brown sugar, eggs, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and salt in a large bowl with an electric mixer until well combined. Pour into the prepared crust.

Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted into the filling 1 inch from the edge comes out clean, 40 to 60 minutes. Cover the edges with foil if needed to prevent from burning as the filling cooks.
Remove from the oven and cool to room temperature before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Fresh Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: This homemade pumpkin pie recipe has a smooth, custardy fresh pumpkin filling with warm spices and a flaky from-scratch crust for a classic Thanksgiving dessert.

video.description: With a from scratch pie crust and rich pumpkin filling, it’s hard to find a better baked dessert than this. In this video, we show you how to make a homemade fresh pumpkin pie for your next holiday gathering.
video.name: How to Make Homemade Fresh Pumpkin Pie

review.reviewBody: This has become a favorite around here. Though, I must agree with others in that it isn't enough to sufficiently fill 2 pie crusts. I have successfully added another 1/2 - 3/4 cup of pumpkin (without adjusting any other ingredients) to help it stretch. Very delish, regardless.

An amazing recipe - not too sweet, not too spicy! Doesn't come out as orange as the photos but delicious nonetheless. Mine was a little runny as well, so I took the advice from another review and added some cornstarch. Mine also didn't make two full pies so I ended up making mini pies in a muffin tin with the leftover filling. Cooked my pie pumpkin in the oven by splitting it in half, cooking at 375 for 45-55 mins, and then pureeing and letting it drain in a cheesecloth + fine mesh strainer. Absolutely give this recipe a shot!! Super simple and perfect for fall 🥰
Made this gluten free and cooked in a convection microwave 25 minutes instead of 40. Added swerve instead of brown sugar, so upped that to 1 cup. Turned out great!

I found the most beautiful white pumpkin on the street. I washed the skin and cut the skin off and cleaned out all the strings. Since I am on a cardiac diet, and because I didn't have all the ingredients, I made adjustments to the recipe. I baked the seeds with onion flakes and garlic powder in olive oil at 375 for 15 minutes for a snack while I worked on the crust free pie. I then pressure cooked the pumpkin meat with a little water for 15 minutes. I drained the water off. I then put it in the food processor. I am on a diet so I left out the crust. I greased a square 9 inch pan. I put all the ingredients together with a bit of gluten free baking mix because I am in high altitude. I substituted eggs with egg whites only, and left out the salt. I didn't have all the spices handy so I used two heaping teaspoons of apple pie spice. I also can't use regular milk so I substituted vanilla almond milk. Thank the Lord, it was just so delicious I can hardly speak. I baked it for more like seventy minutes because of high altitude. It taste a bit like apple pie. It was creamy with a little crust of its own. THANK YOU! I was just so blessed to find the pumpkin. The recipe was helpful to put it all together, thank you very much.

I didn’t follow the recipe exactly. I doubled it, baked the pumpkin for 1 hr at 400 instead of boiling and used one heeping tablespoon of pumpkin pie spice instead of following the spices in the recipe. I also bought premade pie crusts. I got two very full pies and a median ramican worth from doubling it. Thoughts: -this is the best tasting pumpkin pie I have ever had! -the texture is not as silky as when I use canned pumpkin. Next time I will put it in the blender before baking to get a smoother texture. I would 100% recommend this recipe and make it again!

I think the recipe is great, although I add a bit more cinnamon and use fresh nutmeg. My issue is with the pumpkin preparation notes: The key to pumpkin pie is the properties of the pumpkin. The best to use has firm, dense flesh, and low water content. You should never boil pumpkin as it adds water. Instead bake until fork tender. Pumpkin varietal matters, the best are Fairytale, Jarrahdale, and Dickinson- that do not require straining. If you cannot acquire one of these: bake your pumpkin, scoop out the flesh from the rind, and set it in a strainer pushing the excess water out before pureeing.

I made some changes to the original recipe to make it a 5. Instead of fighting with a raw pumpkin, bake the sugar pumpkin whole for about an hour. Let it drain in a strainer in the sink overnight, then cut it and gut it. The skin should peel right off. This gets rid of any excess liquid without adding more. I doubled all the spices, so it was a tsp. each of cinnamon, nutmeg (fresh grated), and ginger, which really ramped up the spice. With the changes, my dad said it was the best pumpkin pie he ever had.

I probably made this pie about ten times with fresh pumpkin. I found it easier to put the gutted cut chunks of pumpkin in a cake pan and put about an inch of water in and put it in the oven at 400 degrees for 30 minutes. I then checked it and moved them around if they weren't all soft and left them for about 15 more minutes. 
The first time I made the pie it turned out a little chunky so I actually blended the pumpkin with some evaporated milk. Then I put it in the fridge for about 30 minutes, then I baked it as directed.

I added my own little twist on this and it came out perfect. I did 1 cup of brown sugar, 3/4 tsp of cinnamon and 1/4 tsp of cloves. Also, dont boil the pumpkin! It comes out tooo watery!
Slice it up and bake it ungreased at 350 for 45 minutes. The skin peels right off, and i prefer no skin in my puree.

This is my go-to recipe. Today I tried it with a ghost pumpkin… (it’s orange on the inside, but seems much sweeter) I used a can of condensed milk instead of evaporated and omit the sugar. Seems very watery, but it turns out nice and light & fluffy the next day or once cooled… I usually reheat it in the oven so I bake it a little less than the full hour too.

This recipe is OK. I recommend the following adjustments: (1) bake instead of boil/steaming the pumpkin otherwise it's too watery and must be strained, (2) cut back the amount of sugar to 1/2 cup, (3) double the amounts of cinnamon, ginger, & nutmeg. NB: Taste your mixture while raw then it's easy to adjust points 2 & 3.

The pie I made looked pale, the mixture was runny, and the images do not reflect what the final result looked like. I followed the recipe to a T, adding a little more pumpkin to match the recipe texture and a little more cinnamon. I don't know what I did wrong, but this is barely edible. Set well though!

This pumpkin pie recipe was so easy to make! I already had a pie crust and pie pumpkin already made, so this recipe went quick. It set up beautifully too. I put it on a cookie sheet and baked it at 425F for 15 mins, then covered with a tinfoil tent, and lowered the temp to 350F for 50 mins, uncovered it for 5 more mins. Perfect!! :)

I have made this pie several times but I use 2 cups of fresh pumpkin as I do not like the strong taste of canned pumpkin...I freeze the shredded or cooked pumpkin ( 2 cups per bag) and have used the frozen for pies, cakes, breads and muffins.

When I use fresh pumpkin after I cook it and puree it, I then put it in a flour sack towel in a sieve and let it drain all the water out. This will really make a big difference. It makes your pumpkin very similar to the canned pumpkin consistency
First time making a pie from scratch! I thought it was great!

Followed the recipe and my pie turned out beautiful . Got great reviews from the family . Will never use canned pumpkin again this was and easy recipe to follow loved the results.....It filled 1 deep dish pie shell perfectly ..

You said to bake at 400 for the whole time, which burnts the crust horribly even after covering it! Never supposed to bake that high the whole time but lower it afer 15 minutes I reminded myself on searching afterwards!!!
Amazing
It was very good and easy to make it also looked amazing I will definitely keep this recipe to use in the future
